packages.label: קִנְאַת הַצַּדִּיק — הַקְּנָאָה לַה' לְבַדּוֹ
packages.label_en: The Tzaddik's Zealousness — Jealousy for God Alone
packages.reason: The phrase 'בְּקַנְּאוֹ אֶת קִנְאָתִי' (Pinchas's act of zealousness for God) and 'הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַנֵּא שׁוּם צַדִּיק, לֹא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְלֹא בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא, רַק אוֹתוֹ לְבַדּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ' share the same essential nature: both express the quality of being zealous exclusively for God and for nothing else. The scriptural phrase IS a bechina of this Tzaddik-quality — they are two faces of the same thing, not cause and effect. Pinchas's act of jealousy for God alone IS the archetypal expression of the Tzaddik who is free from jealousy toward any fellow tzaddik, channeling all his jealousy solely toward the Divine. The polarity is good: this cluster belongs to the domain of holiness and the positive quality of the true Tzaddik.
nodes: הצדיק שאינו מקנא שום צדיק, לא בעולם הזה ולא בעולם הבא, רק אותו לבדו יתברך

good_evil_mirror.mirror_label: קִנְאָה בֵּין צַדִּיקִים — Jealousy Among Tzaddikim
good_evil_mirror.mirror_note: The evil counterpart implied by the Torah is the negative phenomenon of one tzaddik being jealous of another tzaddik — the absence of the quality captured in Package 1. This negative pole (jealousy directed at other tzaddikim rather than at God alone) is the implicit deficiency that the Torah warns against, but it is not explicitly named as a bechina in the text and is not in the dataset for Torah #278.
